To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a synuclein impairs adult neural stem cell proliferation by activating inflammasomes and this impairment is mediated by miRNA 7, which targets a synuclein and NLRP 3.
a synuclein (a-syn) inhibits neurogenesis in mouse adult subventricular zone and adult neural stem cells in vitro, which can be rescued by miR 7 and NLRP 3 knockdown.
a synuclein impairs neurogenesis through NLRP3 activation in mouse subventicular zone, and miR7 is an endogenous inhibitor of NLRP3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of inflammasomes in a synucleinopathy.
the role of inflammasome in adult neurogenesis and the potential mechanisms underlying the impairment of adult neurogenic process by a synuclein.
the role of miR7 in NLRP3-mediated inflammation in adult neural stem cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NLRP3 is a novel target for miR 7, and that NLRP 3 inflammasomes activation may be involved in a synuclein impaired neurogenesis in Parkinson's disease.
miR  7 is a key regulator for NLRP3 expression in ANSCs and miR  5 is a novel therapeutic target for a synuclein induced neuroinflammation in the brain.
a synuclein induced neuroinflammation is a potential pathogenic mechanism of adult neurogenesis impairment in Parkinson's disease, which is mediated via NLRP3 activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a synuclein impairs neurogenesis in the subventricular zone of adult mice through activating NLRP3 and caspase 8 signals in adult neural stem cells.
a synuclein impairs neurogenesis in adult subventricular zone through activating TLR4/Nf kB and NLRp3/caspase1 axis, and miR7 is an important mediator in this process.
